bull.b: RTX's sharp step-up in FCF (TTM +43.8%) signals durable cash-generation from operations and improved conversion versus prior years. This supports reinvestment in capacity, debt reduction and shareholder returns, and provides a buffer to fund multi-year programs and sustain capital-intensive aerospace operations.

A $289B backlog provides multi-year revenue visibility across commercial and defense markets, insulating near-term cyclicality. High defense bookings and an $86B Raytheon backlog underpin sustained production and follow-on sustainment revenue, supporting predictable cash flows and program scale.

Operational improvements at Pratt (MRO ramp, lower AOGs) and Collins' commercial aftermarket strength show execution across diversified segments. Combined defense, commercial OEM and aftermarket exposure reduces single-market risk and boosts margin resiliency as production and services scale.

bear.b: Although debt has declined materially, total leverage remains moderate for the industry. Continued indebtedness leaves less flexibility if large program charges, sustained OE weakness, or defense budget shifts occur, potentially constraining capital allocation or forcing slower deleveraging under stress.

A ~20% gross margin base limits room to absorb raw material, tariff or supply-chain cost inflation without compressing operating profits. In capital-intensive aerospace, constrained gross margin reduces drop-through on revenue gains and increases sensitivity to adverse program mix or production inefficiencies.

Key framework agreements remain unconverted to firm contracts, delaying supplier ramp decisions and revenue recognition. Coupled with planned inventory builds to support higher production, this raises execution and cash-conversion risk if contracting or funding timing shifts, pressuring near-term liquidity metrics.
